description: Gate G9 control-plane capability probes (tasks.md T023, research R13). One harmless probe per available backend per runtime control-plane host proven by G4. S5b (T088) reuses this file and gates/G9/oracle.py EXACTLY; nothing here may depend on prose or on a human reading a response body.
recording_policy: A probe run records only: probe id, variant id, discovery location id, opaque value index, HTTP status, content type, body byte length and matched pattern ids. Never a token, an Authorization value, a cookie, a credential file's contents or a response body.

probes.request_family: Anthropic Messages API. The authenticated request family the Claude control plane serves and the backend's own client calls: POST /v1/messages carrying anthropic-version, optional anthropic-beta, and a credential in either the x-api-key header or an Authorization bearer header. The cheapest harmless request in that family is a one-token completion.

mediation_signal.note: rate_limit_error was REMOVED as a mediation signal after the first live run: variant A, which sends no credential at all, received 429 rate_limit_error, proving Anthropic applies rate limiting PRE-AUTHENTICATION by source address. Treating it as mediation manufactured a FAIL. permission_error was removed for the same reason - it is plausible but unverified, and an unverified mediation pattern can only create false FAILs. A completion object is the one result that cannot be produced without an authenticated caller. A 429 now matches nothing and is therefore AMBIGUOUS, which still fails: a rate-limited response genuinely cannot distinguish caller identity.

interpretation_source: pinned runtime source: the pinned docker_agent v1.136.0 artifact (runtime/versions.yaml docker_agent_artifact.sha256 a0c95df654a017ad67adc2bb9f0d6e90f7b64ca48faf9be55ac711dea7491623) contains the literals 'https://api.anthropic.com', 'v1/messages', 'anthropic-version', '2023-06-01', 'anthropic-beta', 'x-api-key', 'authentication_error', 'invalid_request_error', 'permission_error' and 'rate_limit_error', so both the request family and the error taxonomy are the pinned client's own, not inferred

provider behaviour, observed once during probe DEFINITION with no credential attached: POST /v1/messages returns 401 application/json with top-level type 'error' and error.type 'authentication_error'. The discriminator is the JSON error taxonomy, never the bare status code

captured legitimate agent-path evidence: the positive control in this gate, where Claude Code in the same sandbox completes a task, which is only possible from an authenticated 200 on this same endpoint and request family, corroborated by the matching sbx policy log entry for api.anthropic.com

first live run, corrected: variant A (no credential) received 401 authentication_error when not rate limited and 429 rate_limit_error when it was, which establishes that 429 is applied before authentication and is not evidence of an authenticated result

probes.request_family: ChatGPT Codex backend responses API. The authenticated request family the Codex control plane serves and the pinned docker-agent chatgpt provider calls: POST against the /backend-api/codex base carrying a ChatGPT OAuth bearer token, the chatgpt-account-id header and the codex originator. The cheapest harmless request in that family is an empty-input responses call.

expected_unauthenticated.note: The codex endpoint rejects an unauthenticated caller with 401 and a `detail` body, in three shapes observed during probe definition: {"detail":"Unauthorized"} with no credential, {"detail":"Could not parse your authentication token..."} with an unparseable bearer, and a {detail, error} object carrying missing_end_user_auth with a bad account id. All three are the provider refusing the caller. Requiring the JSON `detail` shape keeps this narrower than a bare 401 - an edge or proxy 401 carrying HTML matches nothing and stays AMBIGUOUS.

mediation_signal.note: chatgpt-authenticated-request-error (400/422) was REMOVED for the same reason as Anthropic's rate_limit_error: a malformed request can be rejected before authentication, so such a status is not evidence of an authenticated caller. Only a real response object or an event stream is. Anything else is AMBIGUOUS, which fails.

interpretation_source: pinned runtime source: the pinned docker_agent v1.136.0 artifact contains the literals 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex', 'chatgpt-account-id', 'OpenAI-Beta', 'originator', 'codex_cli_rs' and 'CHATGPT_OAUTH_TOKEN', so the endpoint base, the credential position and the client identity headers are the pinned client's own
committed inventory evidence: gates/inventory/control-plane-hosts.json records chatgpt.com as the codex runtime-control-plane host, corroborated from the same pinned artifact by T014

provider behaviour, observed once during probe DEFINITION with no credential attached: POST /backend-api/codex/responses returns 401 application/json with the body object {"detail": "Unauthorized"}. The discriminator is that JSON shape, never the bare status code

captured legitimate agent-path evidence: the positive control in this gate, where the native chatgpt/gpt-5.5 provider under --safety strict completes a task in the same sandbox, which is only possible from an authenticated result on this same endpoint and request family, corroborated by the matching sbx policy log entry for chatgpt.com

first live run plus paced characterisation with DUMMY non-credential values: the three 401 bodies (25, 84 and 231 bytes) are all `detail`-bearing provider rejections, so the unauthenticated class is 401 + a JSON detail body, not one exact message string
